text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- NATO military chief supports Spanish mandate of Canary Islands.
- State prosecutor Juan Cesareo Ortiz Urculo openly clashes with prosecution council.
- Supreme court holds that state secrets law does not cover civil servant crimes.
EL MUNDO
- In deciding to declassify some and not all of CESID secret documents, Supreme Court concluded that "security to be preserved is that of state and not of related authorities."
- Group of paleontologists say oldest European human remains found in southern region of Granada.
DIARIO 16
- State prosecutor guards original manuscript and letters from judge Baltasar Garzon in which he proves serious manipulation and changes in summary of "Al Kassar" case.
LA VANGUARDIA
- Europa, one of two small satellites that orbit Jupiter, can locate oceans of water below ice.
ABC
- Supreme Court judge Eduardo Moner notified 15 defendants in kidnap of Segundo Marey, first GAL case, that practiced necessary and adecuate steps and no new, relevant elements exist for hearing.
CINCO DIAS
- Government to analyse on Friday report from Labour ministry on labour reform pact reached between unions and employers and series of measures to strengthen application of reforms.
- Lyonnaise des Eaux will absorb Cie de Suez.
- Vehicle manufacturer Irizar to set up bus manufacturing plant in India.
- Salaries grow 4.5 percent in 1996 and purchasing power grew one percent.
EXPANSION
- Stability plan will limit health spending and cut public aid.
- Telefonica will limit first phase of agreement with BT-MCI in American market in light of difficulties it foresees in global alliance and break of agreements with Unisource and ATT for Europe.
- Industry Ministry wants to place 60 percent of CSI Corporation this year.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Caja de Madrid chairman Miguel Blesa still has not decided where to invest 150 billion pesetas.
- Average salary of worker in 1996 was 208,000 pesetas.
- Convergence plan forecasts social security without deficit in 2000.
